comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1, C2, C7, C8. Both evaluations support the clinical evidence linking WD to poor cholecystitis outcomes. OpenEval notes a potential inconsistency in patient numbers, while peer review highlights this as a key strength without raising this concern.

Perfect agreement on claims C9-C13. Both evaluations support the scRNA-seq methodology and immune cell composition findings. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of data quality metrics, while peer review praises the integration of clinical data and single-cell analyses as solid methods.

Perfect agreement on claims C14-C19. Both evaluations support the detailed immune cell characterization showing enhanced innate immune activation. OpenEval emphasizes multiple converging lines of evidence, while peer review accepts these findings as part of the broader immune microenvironment changes.

Perfect agreement on claims C42-C47. Both evaluations support the orthogonal validation of NK cell exhaustion using mIHC and flow cytometry. OpenEval notes adequate sample sizes and consistency across methodologies, while peer review accepts these as supporting the key NK cell exhaustion findings.

Perfect agreement on claims C49-C54. Both evaluations support the prognostic model development and validation. OpenEval notes the model was not validated in the WD cohort itself, while peer review emphasizes the therapeutic implications and broader applicability to inflammatory and metabolic diseases.

Strong agreement on claims C31-C38 regarding NK cell exhaustion. Both evaluations support the comprehensive molecular evidence. OpenEval notes a paradox requiring mechanistic explanation (increased oxidative phosphorylation alongside exhaustion), while peer review highlights NK cell exhaustion as a key finding without raising this concern. Peer review also includes C39-C40 (transcription factors) in their NK exhaustion assessment.

Strong agreement on claims C20-C24 regarding myeloid cell characterization. Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval focuses specifically on myeloid subtypes, while peer review groups these with broader immune cell characterizations (C25-C28) as part of the immune microenvironment changes.

Agreement on claim C3 regarding ATP7B mutation frequency. Both evaluations support this finding. OpenEval notes the relatively small sample size (n=20) as a limitation, while peer review explicitly identifies this as a key finding and strength without raising sample size concerns.

Partial overlap on claims C4 and C6. Both evaluations support the mechanistic and functional evidence. OpenEval groups C3-C6 together as converging genetic and mechanistic evidence, while peer review focuses on C4 and C6 alongside C56 (background claim) and emphasizes solid methods without specific critique of in vitro data.

Partial agreement on claims C25-C28. Both evaluations support coordinated immune changes. OpenEval notes that opposing MHC class I/II regulation requires further investigation, while peer review accepts these as part of comprehensive immune microenvironment changes without raising this concern.

Agreement on claims C39-C40 regarding transcription factor changes. OpenEval treats these separately as mechanistic support for NK exhaustion, while peer review groups them with the broader NK cell exhaustion findings (C31-C40) as a unified key finding.

Divergent perspectives on claims C1-C2. OpenEval supports the clinical associations, while peer review R10 expresses uncertainty about the causal mechanisms linking ATP7B mutations to cholecystitis, noting it remains unclear whether effects are direct or secondary to liver dysfunction.

Partial overlap on claim C48. OpenEval supports this as literature-based rationale for investigating NK exhaustion in cholecystitis, while peer review R10 questions the mechanistic link between ATP7B mutations and NK cell exhaustion, expressing uncertainty about causality.

Minimal overlap on claim C5 regarding metabolic parameters. OpenEval groups this with genetic evidence (C3-C6), while peer review R11 groups it with C30 as part of the metabolic-immune connection without specific concerns.

Minimal overlap on claim C30 regarding metabolic changes. OpenEval includes this in coordinated immune changes requiring further investigation, while peer review accepts it as part of the metabolic dysfunction-immune dysregulation link.

Agreement on claims C55, C57 as background information. Both evaluations support these as well-established literature-based claims about WD. OpenEval and peer review both accept the background framework without concerns.

Agreement on claims C58-C61 as background information. Both evaluations support these literature-based claims about NK cell biology and exhaustion. OpenEval and peer review both accept this established knowledge framework.

Agreement on claims C62-C65 as background information. Both evaluations support these literature-based claims about liver immunology and cholecystitis. OpenEval and peer review both accept this contextual framework.

Agreement on claims C66-C67 as background information. Both evaluations support these literature-based claims about metabolic regulation of immune function. OpenEval and peer review both accept this contextual framework.

Agreement on claims C68-C70 as background and interpretive information. Both evaluations support these literature-based claims. OpenEval notes some inference about WD mechanisms, while peer review accepts the background framework.

Minimal overlap on claim C56. OpenEval treats this as background on WD pathophysiology, while peer review groups it with mechanistic claims C4 and C6 as part of documenting ATP7B mutation effects on copper metabolism.
OpenEval evaluated claim C71 regarding ethical approval as supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this methodological detail.

Divergent perspectives on claim C36. OpenEval supports this as part of comprehensive NK exhaustion evidence, while peer review R10 expresses uncertainty about the causal mechanisms linking ATP7B mutations to NK cell exhaustion.
